ctrl_16_beam1.note: reproducibility control, re-run hours after 16_beam1. LM reproduced to 0.1% (1356.8 vs 1355.6 ms) and the text exactly; pose moved +9% (3648.7 vs 3336.7). Treat single-run pose timings as +-10%.

findings: Within a run the stages are exactly additive: pose + convert + lm = total to 0.04 ms, so the earlier end-to-end residual is not a within-run accounting gap.
Pose time is invariant to decoder width (3336.7 -> 3414.3 ms, +2.3%, inside run-to-run std) -- the expected independence, and a working internal consistency check.
Pose time is linear in frame count at ~23.7 ms/frame (imread 5.3-5.7, preprocess 4.6-4.9, TRT 11.9-12.8, postprocess 1.19), with ~3% fixed overhead.
Frame rate is the dominant knob: source -> 16 fps at greedy cuts total latency 41.2% (7998 -> 4706 ms) and energy 40.2% (43.11 -> 25.80 J/sentence).
Decoder width is the smaller knob: beam 1 -> beam 4 at 16 fps costs 19.3% latency (+910 ms) and 26.9% energy (+6.95 J/sentence); it lands almost entirely in the LM (+61.1%).

mJ_per_frame RISES under subsampling (169.07 -> 189.70) because the per-sentence LM cost is amortised over fewer frames. Per-frame energy is the wrong denominator for the end-to-end system; per-sentence is the right one.
The pose share of latency falls from 78.3% (src/beam1) to 70.9% (16/beam1) to 60.8% (16/beam4): subsampling moves the bottleneck toward the LM.
memory_finding: TWO separate problems. (a) The LOAD threshold was wrong by 1.3 GB: the full checkpoint load fails at 5214 MB and succeeds from 5268 MB up, a cliff just above 5.2 GB, not the ~4 GB inferred from M1's single success at 4625. A reclaim target of 5000 reaches only ~5200 and straddles it, which failed three cells at load on 10-03. Target is now 6200, guard 5400, and every cell has passed since. (b) source x beam 4 is a genuine working-set limit: three failures, two of them with expandable_segments, which only moved the site to the KV-cache concat, while 24 fps x beam 4 passes at effectively the same MemFree (5757). M1's single success at 4625 MB is the outlier to explain, not a refutation. It does not block the deliverable: that cell is the frontier's ACCURACY reference, measured on the Mac.
scope_limit: n=1 clip, so NO accuracy claim is made. The three outputs are reported only to show that the source-rate decode tracks the reference clause structure most closely; all three miss the content word 'artwork'. The 2x2 interaction term cannot be computed because src_beam4 is missing.
retracted_claim: Two wrong drafts, both recorded. First: 'the first real memory ceiling', concluding frame subsampling is a feasibility requirement for beam search -- refuted by M1. Second: 'a reproducibility failure, not a ceiling' -- too strong in the other direction, since expandable_segments ruled out simple fragmentation and 24 fps passes at the same MemFree. Current reading: a real working-set limit at 255 frames x beam 4, with M1 as the outlier.
frontier_finding: The composition's frame-rate term is well calibrated (source -> 24 fps at greedy measures -16.7% system energy vs -17% predicted), but its decoder-width term is understated 3-5x: measured greedy -> beam 4 costs +7.02 J at 24 fps and +6.95 J at 16 fps, against composed +2.04 and +1.34. The measured penalty is constant in absolute joules across frame rate, as theory says it should be, while the composition makes it grow with T. Cause: frontier.py composes LM_J from RESULTS 2.9C, measured on the PRUNED checkpoint (vocab 26,078), while every end-to-end run loads the FULL released checkpoint (vocab 250,112), and the output projection scales with beams x vocab. A flat 1.255 factor (L4's 69 vs 55 ms/token) puts all three beam-4 cells within +-3% and makes both greedy cells worse, so the right correction is not flat. Decisive experiment: re-run this grid on the pruned checkpoint.
